stories.headline: Glacial collapse triggered Nepal flash floods, not earthquake: USGS
stories.title: Glacial collapse triggered Nepal flash floods, not earthquake: USGS
stories.summary: Washington, Aug 27: The Nepal flash floods were triggered by a glacial collapse and not by a 4.4 magnitude earthquake as reported earlier, the US Geological Survey (USGS) said. The USGS said additional analysis of the long-period seismic waves indicated that the tremors were generated by a glacial collapse and debris flow. The flash floods originating in Tibet on Wednesday left a trail of death and destruction in Rasuwa and Dhading districts of Nepal, killing 162 people and leaving 750, including 133 Indian nationals, missing. “This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred,” the USGS said in an update to its note on the event. It also upgraded the magnitude of the seismic event to 5.2 from the 4.4 assessed earlier. “The USGS determined that the seismic event was a glacial collapse and debris flow that caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream,” it said. Daniel Shugar, an Associate Professor of geomorphology at the University of Calgary in Canada said the flash floods were triggered by a glacier that rolled off a cliff at 5,200 meters. Shugar compared the satellite images of the region taken on Wednesday and Tuesday, a day before the natural disaster struck Nepal. “Comparing satellite imagery from yesterday and today, the glaciers in the vicinity do seem to have lost a fair bit of snow in the last 24 hours,” Shugar was quoted as saying by the New Scientist magazine. “My guess is that snow melt, and glacier ice melt as well, injected a lot of liquid water into the glacier, which percolated down to the bed and lubricated it. That was enough for it to collapse,” he said.

stories.headline: India sends second flight with 37.5 tonnes of aid to flood-hit Nepal
stories.title: India sends second flight with 37.5 tonnes of aid to flood-hit Nepal
stories.summary: New Delhi, Aug 27 : India on Thursday dispatched a second flight carrying 37.5 tonnes of humanitarian supplies, medicines, and food packets to support Nepal's relief efforts after devastating flash floods that have left over 160 dead and hundreds missing. External Affairs Minister (EAM) S. Jaishankar took to X and reaffirmed India's commitment to supporting Nepal in the rescue and relief operations. "A second flight has just taken off, carrying 37.5 tonnes of HADR material, medicines & food packets for Nepal," EAM Jaishankar said in a post on X. "India remains in close and continuous touch with the Nepalese authorities. We will continue to strongly support the ongoing relief efforts," he added. According to the latest official update, the bodies of 162 people swept away by a massive flash flood in Nepal's Bhote Koshi River have been recovered as of Thursday morning. The remains were recovered from riverbanks in several downstream districts along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahu, Nawalparasi (East) and Nawalparasi West, the Police said in a notice. The aid follows a first 10-tonne shipment sent on Wednesday. India's Ambassador to Nepal, Naveen Srivastava, formally handed over the aid consignment to Nepal's Minister of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Khadak Raj Paudel. The assistance includes essential relief materials to help communities affected by widespread flooding and landslides. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India stands firmly with Nepal and remains committed to extending all possible support. The floods in Nepal, triggered by heavy monsoon rains, have caused extensive damage to infrastructure, homes and agricultural land, displacing thousands of families. Rescue and relief operations are ongoing across several provinces, with local authorities struggling to cope with the scale of the disaster. India's assistance comes as part of its longstanding policy of 'Neighbourhood First', under which New Delhi has consistently provided humanitarian aid to neighbouring countries during emergencies. --IANS

stories.headline: Nepal floods: Death toll climbs to 162, search and rescue efforts intensify
stories.title: Nepal floods: Death toll climbs to 162, search and rescue efforts intensify
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Aug 27 : The bodies of 162 people swept away by a massive flash flood in Nepal’s Bhote Koshi River have been recovered as of Thursday morning, Nepal Police said. The remains were recovered from riverbanks in several downstream districts along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahu, Nawalparasi (East) and Nawalparasi West, the Police said in a notice. Most of the bodies were recovered in Chitwan, in Nepal’s southern plains. The massive flood, originating in the Tibetan region, swept through the transboundary Bhote Koshi River, leaving a trail of destruction in Nepal. The Nepali government said that hundreds of people, including foreign nationals, remained out of contact. In a statement issued late Wednesday evening, the Prime Minister’s Office said that 44 Nepal Army personnel, 28 Nepal Police personnel deployed at various police posts and 13 Armed Police Force (APF) personnel working in the affected areas were out of contact. Likewise, 391 foreign tourists and 93 Nepali tourists have remained out of contact following the disaster. The officials have also confirmed that 133 Indians are missing. In addition, 60 employees working at various hydropower projects in the affected areas were reported to be out of contact. This suggests that the death toll from the disaster could rise further. The flood was triggered after an avalanche blocked the flow of the Lhende tributary of the Bhote Koshi River. The flood first hit Timure, near Nepal’s border with China at Rasuwagadhi. Much of the settlement, home to hundreds of people, was swept away before the flood surged downstream, destroying everything in its path. Nepal’s Department of Mines and Geology said it had detected a 4.4-magnitude earthquake, which may have triggered the avalanche. Meanwhile, the Nepali government said on Thursday morning that it had intensified search, rescue and relief operations in riverside and other affected areas following the devastating flood in Rasuwa. “To assist people at risk, the Nepali Army delivered essential relief supplies, including food, tents and medicines, to the affected areas last night,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a notice. Security agencies, along with the private sector, have also provided significant support and cooperation in the rescue and search operations, it said. --IANS

stories.title: Nepal flash floods: SDRF on high alert in Uttarakhand's border district of Champawat
stories.summary: According to officials, apart from the SEOC numbers—0135-2710334, 2710335, 2664314, 2664315, 2664316, and 8218867005—people can also contact the toll-free number 1070
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Vigilance has been stepped up in Uttarakhand's border district of Champawat following severe floods in Nepal on Wednesday (August 26, 2026).
The Tanakpur post of the SDRF has been placed on high alert, and people have been urged to stay away from the banks of the Sharda River, officials said.
According to officials, the Tanakpur post in Champawat district has been put on high alert under the instructions of State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) Commandant Arpan Yaduvanshi.
The SDRF's Tanakpur team is continuously monitoring and patrolling vulnerable riverbank areas, including the Sharda Ghat, the Sharda Barrage, and surrounding localities.
The team is keeping a close watch on the river's water level and potential risks while maintaining coordination with the local administration.
Officials said that the SDRF team visited the Sharda Ghat and low-lying areas to alert local residents, travellers and fishermen about the potential rise in the river's water level.
People have been urged not to venture near the riverbanks unnecessarily under any circumstances and to adhere to safety guidelines issued by the administration.
They added that the SDRF team is fully prepared round-the-clock with essential life-saving and rescue equipment to initiate immediate relief and rescue operations in the event of any emergency.
The Uttarakhand government has also issued helpline numbers to assist the state’s people stranded there.
Officials said that the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority (USDMA) has released these helpline numbers to aid the people.

If any person from Uttarakhand is stranded in the affected area of Nepal, or if anyone wishes to share information regarding an individual, they can contact the helpline numbers of the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) in Dehradun.
According to officials, apart from the SEOC numbers—0135-2710334, 2710335, 2664314, 2664315, 2664316, and 8218867005—people can also contact the toll-free number 1070.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay, Minister Aadhav Arjuna Move High Court Seeking Rejection Of Election Petitions Challenging Their 2026 Poll Victory
stories.title: Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay, Minister Aadhav Arjuna Move High Court Seeking Rejection Of Election Petitions Challenging Their 2026 Poll Victory
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay and Minister Aadhav Arjuna have filed applications to reject the election petitions challenging their victory during the 2026 Legislative Assembly Elections.
Justice V Lakshminarayanan was informed that the applications have been filed and the same are yet to be numbered.
The court has asked the petitions to be listed on Friday (August 28) and Monday (August 31).
The court had, on Tuesday (August 25), warned that it would impose costs on the CM and the Minister if they continued to take adjournments in the pleas.
When the counsels had informed the court that the applications were ready and sought a day's time to file the same, the court refrained from imposing costs and adjourned the hearing by a day.
Following this, when the election petitions were taken up for hearing, the court was informed that the applications were filed but were yet to be numbered.
The court was also given details of the filing number.

It may be noted that in July this year, the court had admitted election petitions challenging the victory of Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Joseph Vijay, from the Perambur and Trichy (east) constituencies during the 2026 assembly elections.
The court also admitted election petitions challenging the victory of Tamil Nadu Sports Minister Aadhav Arjuna from the Villivakkam constituency.
While permitting private notice in the case, the Judge had emphasised that election petitions were required to be decided as expeditiously as possible, within 6 months.
Later, both Aadhav Arjuna and the Chief Minister had informed the court that they intended to file applications for rejecting the election petitions.
When the case was taken up previously, the court had granted two weeks' time and had asked the parties to ensure that the applications are filed within time.

stories.headline: Karnataka to declare 101 taluks drought-hit as 32 more remain under review
stories.title: Karnataka to declare 101 taluks drought-hit as 32 more remain under review
stories.summary: The Karnataka government has decided to declare 101 taluks drought-hit, while another 32 that have met the initial eligibility criteria are being reassessed, Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G Parameshwara said on Thursday.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Karnataka government has decided to declare 101 taluks drought-hit, while another 32 that have met the initial eligibility criteria are being reassessed, Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G Parameshwara said on Thursday.
Addressing a press conference at Vidhana Soudha, Parameshwara described the current conditions as unprecedented and said the government was spending Rs 635 crore on drought management.
He maintained that there was no shortage of funds to protect residents and livestock from the impact of the rainfall deficit.
Karnataka received 465 mm of rain between 1 June and 26 August against the normal 666 mm, resulting in a deficit of 30 per cent.
Twenty-nine districts and 190 taluks have recorded deficient to large-deficient rainfall, while 12 taluks are experiencing a severe shortfall.
As of 26 August, 134 taluks had witnessed dry spells lasting more than three consecutive weeks, making them eligible for an assessment under Trigger-1 of the Centre’s Drought Manual, 2020.
The state subsequently carried out ground verification using the prescribed assessment parameters and found 101 taluks eligible to be declared drought-hit.
Another 32 taluks that qualified under Trigger-1 are being reassessed.
The conditions in the 101 taluks will be reviewed every 15 days after the formal declaration.
Similar verification has been conducted at the hobli level, and the data is being examined.
Under the drought manual, Trigger-1 applies to areas experiencing dry spells of at least three consecutive weeks.
Trigger-2 assesses sowing coverage, crop health, soil moisture, groundwater levels and water availability in tanks and reservoirs.

stories.headline: Tata Power's $640-Million Singapore Problem
stories.title: Tata Power's $640-Million Singapore Problem
stories.summary: India's largest integrated private power utility has run out of road in Singapore's courts, at least for now. On August 26, 2026, the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) dismissed every application Tata Power had filed to overturn a $490.32 million arbitration award won by Kleros Capital Partners, a UK-based investment firm. The court rejected both of Tata Power's core arguments: that the tribunal's damages calculation (quantum) was wrong, and that the majority's decision-making process had breached natural justice. With interest accruing since November 2020 and legal costs added on, the total bill has now crossed $640 million, or upwards of ₹6,000 crore. Tata Power's shares fell as much as 5% in the following session, and the company has confirmed it will appeal to the Singapore Court of Appeal. The market cap loss from today's fall roughly matches the full quantum of the firm' liabilities from the award, indicating how quickly the market has priced in the liability and the uncertainty linked to it. How the dispute began The roots of the case go back to a coal partnership in Russia that never materialised. Kleros initiated arbitration proceedings against Tata Power at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) in November 2020, alleging that Tata Power had breached confidentiality and non-circumvention obligations tied to a proposed joint pursuit of the Krutogorovo coal project in Russia. A three-member tribunal — Professor Lawrence Boo (presiding), Stuart Isaacs KC, and retired Indian Supreme Court judge Amal K. Ganguli heard the matter. In September 2023, the panel unanimously found Tata Power liable, concluding that the company had misused confidential information, deliberately circumvented Kleros, made misleading statements, and concealed material facts in order to pursue the project on its own account. Liability was never in question after that point, only the size of the damages. In July 2025, the tribunal issued its award on quantum. Here the panel split 2:1: Boo and Isaacs, in the majority, awarded Kleros $490.32 million plus simple interest of 5.33% per annum from November 30, 2020, until payment. All three arbitrators agreed Tata Power owed something; they differed only on methodology and amount. Rather than resisting enforcement, Tata Power took the award to the Singapore courts directly, challenging both the quantum and the fairness of the tribunal's process. That challenge is what the SICC dismissed on August 26. What happens next Tata Power has said it will file an appeal with the Singapore Court of Appeal within the mandatory 28-day window from the SICC's order. But this is a narrower and steeper climb than the challenge just rejected. Appellate review of arbitration-related court decisions is deliberately constrained. International arbitration is designed around finality, and courts at the seat of arbitration (Singapore, in this case) generally give tribunals wide deference on quantum and process once liability has been unanimously established. The more immediate complication: filing an appeal does not automatically pause enforcement. Unless Tata Power secures an explicit stay from the Singapore courts, Kleros is free to pursue enforcement of the award in Singapore or in other jurisdictions where Tata Power or its group entities hold assets while the appeal plays out. That makes the coming weeks less about the legal argument and more about interim relief: whether Tata Power can buy itself time without the liability crystallising into an immediate cash call. Does this set a precedent? The SICC's order turns on the specific facts of this arbitration rather than announcing a broad legal principle. But it is a useful data point for Indian companies increasingly exposed to international commercial arbitration on cross-border deal conduct, not just contract non-performance. Two things stand out. First, allegations around confidentiality, circumvention, and misuse of shared information are treated seriously by arbitral tribunals and are hard to unwind on appeal once liability is unanimous. Second, seat courts like Singapore's, much like London's or Hong Kong's set a high bar for "natural justice" and "quantum" challenges, making them a weak lever once an award has been issued by a properly constituted panel. stories.headline: J&K Deputy CM says Congress likely to join government soon, attacks BJP over ‘discrimination’ against Jammu
stories.title: J&K Deputy CM says Congress likely to join government soon, attacks BJP over ‘discrimination’ against Jammu
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 27: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary said on Thursday that the Congress is expected to join the National Conference-led government soon, describing the move as a natural development given the two parties’ alliance. Choudhary said the National Conference had wanted Congress to become part of the government since the alliance was formed, but that the final decision had rested with the Congress. “As far as Congress is concerned, ever since this government was formed, when we entered into the alliance, it was our desire and we wanted Congress to join,” he said. “But Congress was unable to take a decision. Now Congress is taking a decision, and I think everyone should be happy because it is an alliance partner.” He said Congress joining the government would strengthen the administration and help it deliver for the people. “If Congress also comes in, the government will run with greater strength and we will be able to work for the people,” Choudhary said. “Because it is our alliance partner, they have a right to come into the government.” Asked what the National Conference was offering Congress, including the number of ministerial berths, Choudhary rejected the suggestion that the party was negotiating through inducements. “We are not BJP people. We are not like the BJP people who do horse-trading,” he said. “These are relationships of the heart. We are people who connect hearts, and decisions taken from the heart last long and are for the betterment of the people.” He added: “It does not happen that we will bring someone by giving them greed or temptation. This is the work of the BJP.” Deputy CM attacks BJP over Jammu ‘discrimination’ Choudhary also launched a broadside against the BJP, accusing it of failing to address what he described as discrimination against Jammu. Responding to BJP claims that a cabinet reshuffle could bring down the government, he said the BJP should focus instead on issues affecting the region. He questioned why, according to him, there was no Jammu-based professor serving as vice-chancellor at any of Jammu’s universities and why no local doctor had become director of AIIMS. “Is this not discrimination that professors and doctors from Jammu do not have the right to become vice-chancellors or directors?” he asked. “Are our professors so incompetent? Are our doctors so incompetent that they cannot become vice-chancellors? Can they not become directors of AIIMS, IIM or IIT?” He urged the media in Jammu to question the BJP on these issues rather than focus on the National Conference. “Tell them not to talk about things here and there. Tell them why discrimination against Jammu is still not ending,” he said. Choudhary also alleged that Jammu’s business sector was suffering and challenged the BJP to explain how it planned to revive trade and industry in the region. He referred to the ₹28,000-crore industrial package for Jammu and Kashmir and questioned whether existing industries in Jammu had benefited from it. “Go to the Gangyal Industrial Estate, go to Bari Brahmana Industrial Estate, go to Samba, go to Kathua and wherever our industrial estates are,” he said. “Ask whether the old industries of Jammu and Kashmir have received anything from the package. Nothing has been given.” Power tariffs, inflation and cost of living The Deputy Chief Minister also defended the government on electricity tariffs, arguing that the issue should be viewed against the record of the previous BJP-PDP administration. “You should compare the last 12 years,” he said. “Find out how much electricity rates increased during the BJP period and how high electricity bills were.” He also pointed to the government’s electricity amnesty measures and challenged the BJP to answer questions about the rising prices of basic commodities. “Ask the BJP people how much sugar costs. Is it ₹70 or ₹75 a kilo?” he said. “Ask them how much pulses cost. Ask them the price of vegetables and onions.” Choudhary said the impact of inflation was particularly severe on ordinary households. “For a poor man who has only one bulb, what does he know whether the bill is bigger or smaller?” he said. “He knows the price of the sugar he needs for his tea.” He also accused the BJP of failing to address rising education and healthcare costs. “Ask them why fees in universities have increased,” he said. “Ask them about the fees in hospitals. These are important issues.” ‘We will take back Article 370 and statehood’ On Article 370 and statehood, Choudhary said the National Conference remained committed to restoring Jammu and Kashmir’s special status and statehood. “We will take back 370. We will take back special status. We will protect our children’s jobs and will not allow our poor people’s land to be taken by outsiders,” he said. He argued that the BJP had itself made commitments regarding employment and land during the parliamentary debate following the 2019 changes. “This was a promise made by the BJP,” Choudhary said. “It was said in Parliament that the jobs of Jammu and Kashmir would not be taken by outsiders and the land of the people of Jammu and Kashmir would not be taken by outsiders.” He said the BJP therefore had an even greater responsibility to address the issues of special status and statehood. ‘Stop counting the sacrifices of children’ Choudhary also criticised BJP leader Ashok Kaul over remarks concerning the number of BJP children who had died during militancy. He said the deaths of young people should not be turned into a political calculation. “A child may belong to a poor family, a child may be a BJP worker’s child, a child may be from the National Conference, PDP, Congress or any other party, or even an ordinary person’s child—if someone is killed in militancy, it is a matter of great sorrow,” he said. “What kind of counting is this that you have started, Ashok Kaul sahib?” he asked. He also questioned BJP leaders over their participation, or that of their children, in the Ram temple movement and said political leaders should stop comparing sacrifices. “Stop talking about the sacrifices and martyrdom of children,” he said, urging the BJP to instead answer questions about Jammu and Kashmir. BJP challenged over unemployment and vacant posts Choudhary further challenged the BJP to explain its record on unemployment and the regularisation of temporary workers. Ahead of the BJP’s proposed September 2 protest at the Civil Secretariat, he asked the party to explain why vacant posts had not been filled over the past 12 years. “Ask them why they did not fill them,” he said, referring to vacant government posts. He also questioned why various categories of temporary workers—including SPOs, Home Guards, daily wagers and workers associated with horticulture, agriculture and other departments—had not been regularised. “They talk about unemployment. Ask them, you had promised that you would provide two crore jobs,” Choudhary said. “Of that two crore, what share did Jammu and Kashmir get?” He also invoked the BJP’s earlier promise of depositing ₹15 lakh in people’s bank accounts, saying the party should fulfil that promise before coming to the Civil Secretariat. ‘We are politicians; we move towards the destination’ On speculation about internal divisions within the National Conference and whether political developments could affect the party, Choudhary said his focus remained on fulfilling the commitments made to the people. “We are politicians. We move towards the destination,” he said. “We do not calculate into plus or minus. We know that the destination is in front of us, and that destination is one—to work for the welfare of the people and fulfil the promises we have made.” Choudhary also dismissed suggestions that he was afraid of the BJP, pointing out that he had previously defeated its state president. “If I was afraid of the BJP, I would not have left after defeating its state president,” he said.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently stayed the order passed by the Bar Council of India permanently debarring Madhya Pradesh-based advocate and former judicial officer, Narendra Kumar Jain, from practising law over his alleged unwarranted remarks on the judiciary.

A bench comprising Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta stayed the BCI's order, which had found him guilty of professional misconduct over allegations of making remarks against the judiciary and judges.
The bench also issued notice to the BCI on Jain's appeal.
Challenging the BCI's order, the petitioner, in his plea, claimed that he was not given an opportunity to defend himself, violating the principles of natural justice.
Senior Advocate Vivek Tankha appeared for the former judicial officer, and based on his submissions, the bench stayed the BCI's order.

stories.headline: Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova, other power capex stocks rise up to 5%. Two reasons behind the surge
stories.title: Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova, other power capex stocks rise up to 5%. Two reasons behind the surge
stories.summary: Shares of power capex stocks such as CG Power, GE Vernova, TD Power, Siemens rallied up to 5% after chip giant Nvidia reported a staggering 117% jump in data centre revenue year-on-year at $89 billion in the second quarter, alongside stellar 2028 guidance.In today’s session, TD Power shares jumped 5% to Rs 765 per share, while GE Vernova TD India gained over 4% to Rs 4,535. CG Power shares rose over 2% to Rs 899 per share, while Siemens also rose over 2% to Rs 4,137 per share. Hitachi India shares rose over 3% to Rs 34,248 per share.1.) What did Nvidia say about data centres?Nvidia announced strategic partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish independent compute-financing platforms. The platforms are expected to mobilise more than $500 billion of third-party capital over time for the buildout of AI infrastructure, subject to definitive agreements.The company also expanded Korea's AI factory ecosystem through strategic partnerships with SK Telecom, NAVER and Brookfield. The partnerships will support the development of sovereign AI infrastructure at gigawatt scale on the NVIDIA DSX platform, as part of a broader Nvidia-powered national AI push across Korea's industries and research institutions.AI data centres need enormous amounts of electricity and the equipment required to transmit, convert and manage that power. So, when Nvidia signals that hyperscalers, AI labs and other customers are continuing to spend heavily on AI infrastructure, investors extrapolate that demand into the power-equipment supply chain.2.) US bans Chinese power equipment manufacturersUS President Donald Trump on Wednesday signed an executive order declaring a national emergency over foreign-made equipment used in the U.S. electricity grid and banning the use of certain such equipment, the White House said.The order points to what the White House called an "unusual and extraordinary foreign threat" from foreign-made bulk-power systems that could create national security vulnerabilities.The move is the latest step by Washington to address technology threats it associates with China. It follows a decision by the European Commission earlier this year to prohibit Chinese-made inverters from publicly funded energy projects.Under Trump's order, certain foreign-produced bulk-power system equipment will be prohibited from being purchased or installed in the United States. The ban also covers associated critical software and digital capabilities that could create cybersecurity or operational risks, according to the White House.The order further directs the U.S. Energy Secretary to set conditions for the continued use and operation of such equipment in order to address concerns identified by the Trump administration, the White House said.Nvidia Q2 resultsNvidia shares jumped 5% in extended trading on Wednesday after the world's most valuable company reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 results that came in ahead of analyst expectations. The order points to what the White House called an "unusual and extraordinary foreign threat" from foreign-made bulk-power systems that could create national security vulnerabilities.

The ban also covers associated critical software and digital capabilities that could create cybersecurity or operational risks, according to the White House.

stories.title: India, China, Canada & more: 10 countries still under Trump’s tariff squeeze and why
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: From India and Canada to Iran and Venezuela, the countries may be thousands of miles apart and have little in common economically.

Yet they have found themselves facing the same problem: an unpredictable US trade policy under President Donald Trump, in which tariffs and sanctions are being deployed for reasons that go beyond conventional trade disputes.

Trade deficits remain a key justification for many measures, but Trump has increasingly tied economic pressure to wars, Russian oil, fentanyl, immigration, deportations, drug trafficking, nuclear programmes and even the domestic policies of US allies.

That sequence of threaten, negotiate, delay, collapse talks, retaliate and threaten further escalation has become a defining feature of Trump's approach, making the tariff regime difficult for governments and businesses to predict.
Canada has emerged as one of the clearest and most recently escalated examples of how Trump's trade policy has expanded beyond trade.

In the latest, Ottawa announced 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion of US goods, effective September 8, matching Washington's measures “dollar for dollar, rate for rate.”
The tariffs cover steel, dairy, seafood, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics and other goods.
Canada also announced a C$7.5 billion support package for affected workers and businesses.
The move followed Trump's 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed.
But the dispute has long involved more than trade.
In 2025, Trump repeatedly cited fentanyl trafficking and illegal immigration, accusing Ottawa of failing to secure the northern border, while also alleging discriminatory treatment of US products.
The negotiations brought in another non-trade issue.
